title: Reefer Cargo Services: uniform tier, commodity and set point across one booking
content:
## Scope

Under **Reefer Cargo Services**, the reefer services of one booking are held together. This rule applies at two moments: when a new reefer service is ordered on a booking, and when the carrying settings of a service are changed.

## Rule

1. Every live service on a booking (live meaning not cancelled) must carry the same tier, the same commodity and the same set point, because one booking moves one commodity under one set of carrying instructions.
2. A new service, or a setting change, that would break this uniformity is refused.
3. The customer changes all services of the booking together, and each change is recorded on each service.
4. Uniformity is judged from the company's service records for that booking before the order or change is made; the booking of the request is the booking whose live services are compared.

## What must match, and what the rule does not name

| Attribute | Must be identical across live services of the booking? |
|---|---|
| Tier (for example AHL Reefer Monitored) | Yes |
| Commodity | Yes |
| Set point | Yes |

The rule names only these three attributes as the uniformity test.

## Hypothetical cases

> **Case 1, new order.** A booking has two live services under AHL Reefer Cold Treatment carrying fresh table grapes at 0.5 °C. A third service is requested for the same booking under the same tier, the same commodity and 0.5 °C. Uniformity holds.

> **Case 2, new order that breaks uniformity.** For the same booking, a third service is requested under AHL Reefer Monitored. The tier differs from the live services, so the new service is refused.

> **Case 3, change on one container only.** A booking has three live services at 4.0 °C and the shipper asks to move only one container to 2.0 °C. The live services would no longer share one set point, so the change is refused.

> **Case 4, change on all containers.** The shipper instead instructs the change to 2.0 °C for all three services of the booking together. Uniformity holds, and the change is recorded on each of the three services.

> **Case 5, a cancelled service.** A booking holds one live service at 4.0 °C and one cancelled service that had been ordered at 8.0 °C. The cancelled service is not live and is not part of the comparison.

## Points of judgement

**A customer asks to change "just the one container that is warming up". Can the desk do this for that container alone?** Not where the booking has other live services: the change must apply to all services of the booking together, each change recorded on each service.
